title: Low-degree monomials multilinearize on the root cube
statement: Let $K$ be a field and let $\omega \in K$ satisfy $\omega \ne 1$. Fix $n, D \in \bbn$, and consider a monomial $a\,X^m$ in the variables $X_1,\dots,X_n$ over $K$, given by an exponent vector $m : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbn$ and a coefficient $a \in K$, whose total degree $\sum_i m_i$ is at most $D$. Then there exist coefficients $c : \mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K$, indexed by the squarefree supports $s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ with $\abs{s} \le D$, such that the squarefree polynomial $\sum_{\abs{s} \le D} c(s)\prod_{i \in s} X_i$ takes the same value as $a\,X^m$ at every point $x$ of the root cube $\{1,\omega\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: total degree of the monomial (sum of exponents) is at most D
n and D are natural numbers
arbitrary coefficient a in K and exponent vector m
replaced:
Assume $\omega \ne 1$.  If a monomial $a\,X^m$ has total exponent sum
$\sum_i m_i \le D$, then it agrees on the root cube $\{1,\omega\}^n$ with a squarefree
polynomial built only from supports of size at most $D$: there exist coefficients
$c$ on $\texttt{ACP.LowDegreeSupport}\ n\ D$ with
$(\texttt{ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial}\ c)(x) = (a\,X^m)(x)$ for every $x$ in the cube.
